_note: The `files` module's PURE CORE: the root vocabulary, the per-platform physical base each token maps to, path normalisation, and the two containment checks that ARE the sandbox. This is a security boundary, not a convenience: a path that escapes its root is refused, and every renderer must refuse it the same way, so the corpus is the law and the three runners (TS files-conformance.test.ts, Kotlin FilesPathConformanceTest, Swift DSXFilePaths) execute this one file. parse[] pins the TEXTUAL half — a `root:relative` document path is trimmed, its root matched EXACT CASE against the closed five-word vocabulary, and its relative part normalised (`.` dropped, `..` popped, empty segments collapsed) BEFORE the escape test, because checking before normalisation is the classic bypass. contains[] pins the PHYSICAL half — after a facet has asked the OS to resolve symlinks (realpath), it asks here whether the resolved path is still inside the resolved base; `/a/bc` is NOT inside `/a/b`, which is the prefix-without-separator bug that every hand-rolled check ships at least once. Every refusal is `unsupported_root`: a path this module will not address is one condition with one code, whatever shape the attempt took (parity/F03-files.md §3a, §3c).
_note_bases: The physical base each token resolves to, as a PLATFORM TOKEN rather than a container path — the container path is a runtime value (an app group id, an OPFS handle), the CHOICE of directory is the decision, and the decision is what has to agree on three renderers. A null base is the typed absence: the platform has no such place, so the facet resolves `unsupported_platform` rather than inventing one. `writable:false` is the read-only root: a write/mkdir/delete/move-to against it is `permission_denied`, never a silent no-op.

_note_glob: `list`'s `glob` filter, matched against the path RELATIVE to the listed directory with `/` separators. A tiny, closed grammar on purpose: `*` matches any run of characters within one segment, `?` matches one character within one segment, and a whole segment of `**` matches zero or more segments. Brace expansion, character classes and negation are deliberately absent - they are where every hand-rolled matcher starts disagreeing with every other, and a listing filter needs none of them. The match is anchored (the whole relative path, not a substring) and case-exact. Three facets would otherwise each grow their own matcher, which is exactly the drift the unified-codebase law exists to stop.

_note_contains: The PHYSICAL half, run AFTER the OS has resolved symlinks on both sides. The facet realpaths the base and the candidate and asks this; a symlink inside a root that points anywhere else therefore fails here rather than being followed silently. Both sides must be absolute; comparison is byte-exact (a case-insensitive filesystem does not make `/A/B` the same sandbox as `/a/b` for our purposes — a mismatch means the facet resolved something it did not expect, which is exactly when to refuse).
